at underskrive.explanation: "At underskrive" means "to sign". It is built from "under" (under) and "at skrive" (to write), because you write your name under the text. To say you sign an agreement, use it with the agreement: "Jeg underskriver aftalen" (I sign the agreement). The same meaning can be said with "at skrive under" (to sign): "Skriv under her" (Sign here).

at understrege.explanation: "At understrege" means "to emphasize". It is built from "under" (under) and "streg" (a line), so you put a line under a point. When you draw a line under written words, it means "to underline": "Understreg ordet" (Underline the word).

at understøtte.explanation: "At understøtte" means "to support". When you back an idea with facts, use it with the idea: "Tallene understøtter hans teori" (The numbers support his theory). When a program or device can work with something, use it for that: "Programmet understøtter flere sprog" (The program supports several languages).

at undersøge.explanation: "At undersøge" means "to examine / investigate". It is built from "under" (under) and "at søge" (to search). To say a doctor checks a patient, use it with the patient: "Lægen undersøger mig" (The doctor examines me).

at undertrykke.explanation: "At undertrykke" means "to suppress / oppress". When you hold in a feeling or a sound, use it with that feeling: "undertrykke et gab" (suppress a yawn). When a group of people is kept down by force or unfair rules, use it with the group: "Regimet undertrykker mindretallet" (The regime oppresses the minority).

at undervise.explanation: "At undervise" means "to teach". To say which subject you teach, add "i" (in) before it: "Hun underviser i matematik" (She teaches math). The person who learns uses a different verb, "at lære" (to learn): "Jeg lærer dansk" (I am learning Danish).

at undervurdere.explanation: "At undervurdere" means "to underestimate". It is built from "under" (under) and "at vurdere" (to assess), so you rate something too low. To warn someone, say: "Undervurder ikke opgaven" (Do not underestimate the task).

at undgå.explanation: "At undgå" means "to avoid". To say you stay away from a food, use it with that food: "Jeg undgår sukker" (I avoid sugar). To say you stop something from happening, use "at forhindre" (to prevent) instead: "Vi forhindrer ulykken" (We prevent the accident).

at undlade.explanation: "At undlade" means "to omit". To say you leave a word or a detail out of a text, use "at udelade" (to leave out) instead: "Jeg udelader navnet" (I leave out the name).

at undre sig.explanation: "At undre sig" means "to wonder". To name the thing that surprises you, add "over" (about): "Jeg undrer mig over prisen" (I am surprised at the price). To ask yourself a question, use "Jeg gad vide" (I wonder): "Jeg gad vide, hvad klokken er" (I wonder what time it is).

at undskylde.explanation: "At undskylde" means "to apologize". The short word "Undskyld" means "Sorry" when you made a mistake: "Undskyld, jeg kom for sent" (Sorry, I was late). It means "Excuse me" when you want someone's attention: "Undskyld, hvor er toilettet?" (Excuse me, where is the toilet?). To name the mistake you apologize for, add "for" (for): "Jeg undskylder for forsinkelsen" (I apologize for the delay).

at undslippe.explanation: "At undslippe" means "to escape". To say what you escape from, put the thing right after it, with no word for "from": "undslippe faren" (escape the danger).

at undvære.explanation: "At undvære" means "to do without". To say you need something every day, use it with "ikke" (not): "Jeg kan ikke undvære min telefon" (I cannot do without my phone). To ask if someone can spare something for a while, use it in a question: "Kan du undvære bilen i dag?" (Can you spare the car today?)

at uploade.explanation: "At uploade" means "to upload". It is borrowed from the English word "upload". To tell someone to upload something, use the short command form: "Upload dokumentet her" (Upload the document here).

en ubalance.explanation: "En ubalance" means "an imbalance". The start "u-" turns a word into its opposite, as in "uvenlig" (unfriendly). To say where things are out of balance, add "i" (in): "en ubalance i økonomien" (an imbalance in the economy).

en ubåd.explanation: "En ubåd" means "a submarine". It is short for "en undervandsbåd" (literally, an underwater boat).

en udbetaling.explanation: "En udbetaling" means "a payout". It is built from "ud" (out) and "en betaling" (a payment). When you buy a home, it also means the down payment: "en udbetaling på 200.000 kroner" (a down payment of 200,000 kroner).

en uddannelse.explanation: "En uddannelse" means "an education". To say you are training for a job, use it with "at tage" (to take): "Hun tager en uddannelse som sygeplejerske" (She is training to be a nurse).

en udenrigsminister.explanation: "En udenrigsminister" means "a foreign minister". The start "udenrigs-" means "foreign", as in "udenrigspolitik" (foreign policy).

en udenrigsrejse.explanation: "En udenrigsrejse" means "a trip abroad". It is built from "udenrigs" (foreign) and "en rejse" (a journey). The start "udenrigs-" is also in "udenrigsminister" (foreign minister).

en udflugt.explanation: "En udflugt" means "an excursion". It is built from "ud" (out) and "flugt" (escape). To say where the group is right now, use "på" (on): "Børnene er på udflugt" (The children are on an excursion).

en udfordring.explanation: "En udfordring" means "a challenge". It comes from "at udfordre" (to challenge). To say you face one, use "at stå over for" (to face): "Vi står over for en ny udfordring" (We face a new challenge).

en udgang.explanation: "En udgang" means "an exit". On a highway, use "en afkørsel" (an exit ramp) instead: "Tag næste afkørsel" (Take the next exit).

en udgave.explanation: "En udgave" means "an edition", as in a printing of a book. It also means "a version" of something, such as a film: "Jeg har set den nye udgave af filmen" (I have seen the new version of the film).

en udgift.explanation: "En udgift" means "an expense". Its opposite is "en indtægt" (an income): "Vi har flere udgifter end indtægter" (We have more expenses than income). To talk about costs that stay the same every month, use "faste udgifter" (fixed expenses).

en udgivelse.explanation: "En udgivelse" means "a release". Do not mix it up with "en udgave" (an edition). To talk about the date something comes out, use "udgivelse": "Udgivelsen af albummet blev udsat" (The release of the album was postponed). To say which version of a book you have, use "udgave": "Jeg har den danske udgave" (I have the Danish edition).

en udklædning.explanation: "En udklædning" means "a costume". It comes from "at klæde sig ud" (to dress up). To say you dress up as something, use "som" (as): "Jeg klæder mig ud som pirat" (I dress up as a pirate). In Denmark, children wear a costume at "fastelavn" (a holiday in February or March).

en udlejer.explanation: "En udlejer" means "a landlord". It comes from the verb "at udleje" (to rent out). To say you rent out your home, use the verb: "Jeg udlejer min lejlighed" (I rent out my apartment).

en udlejningsbil.explanation: "En udlejningsbil" means "a rental car". It is built from "udlejning" (renting out) and "bil" (car). The word "udlejning" is in other words too, as in "cykeludlejning" (bike rental).

en udlånstid.explanation: "En udlånstid" means "a loan period". It is built from "udlån" (lending out) and "tid" (time). To ask how long you may keep a book, say: "Hvad er udlånstiden?" (What is the loan period?)

en udlænding.explanation: "En udlænding" means "a foreigner". It is built from "ud" (out) and "et land" (a country), like "udlandet" (abroad).

en udnævnelse.explanation: "En udnævnelse" means "an appointment", as in being named to a job or title. To talk about a meeting with a doctor, use "en aftale" (an appointment) instead: "Jeg har en aftale hos lægen i morgen" (I have an appointment at the doctor tomorrow).

en udryddelse.explanation: "En udryddelse" means "an extinction". To say pests are wiped out on purpose, add "af" (of) and the pests: "en udryddelse af rotter" (an extermination of rats).

en udsendelse.explanation: "En udsendelse" means "a broadcast". When a soldier or aid worker is sent to work abroad, it means "deployment": "Hans udsendelse varer seks måneder" (His deployment lasts six months).

en udsigt.explanation: "En udsigt" means "a view". When you talk about what is expected to happen, it means "prospect" and is used with "til" (of): "Der er udsigt til regn" (Rain is expected).

en udskiftning.explanation: "En udskiftning" means "a replacement", as in swapping an old part for a new one. It is built from "ud" (out) and "at skifte" (to change). To say you swap something out, use "at skifte ud" (to swap out): "Vi skifter dækkene ud" (We swap the tires out).

en udskrivning.explanation: "En udskrivning" means "a discharge (from hospital)". It comes from the verb "at udskrive" (to discharge). To say a patient is allowed to go home, use the verb: "Han bliver udskrevet i morgen" (He is being discharged tomorrow).

en udstilling.explanation: "En udstilling" means "an exhibition". It comes from the verb "at udstille" (to exhibit). To say a museum shows something, use the verb: "Museet udstiller hans billeder" (The museum exhibits his paintings).

en udstrækning.explanation: "En udstrækning" means "a stretch", as in loosening your muscles. When you talk about how far something goes, it means "extent": "i stor udstrækning" (to a large extent).

en udstødning.explanation: "En udstødning" means "an exhaust", as on a car. When a person is pushed out of a group, it means "exclusion": "social udstødning" (social exclusion).

en udtale.explanation: "En udtale" means "a pronunciation". It comes from the verb "at udtale" (to pronounce). To ask how to say a word, use the verb: "Hvordan udtaler man ordet?" (How do you pronounce the word?)

en udtalelse.explanation: "En udtalelse" means "a statement". To say someone gave an official statement, say: "Direktøren afgav en udtalelse til pressen" (The director gave a statement to the press). Do not mix it up with "en udtale" (a pronunciation). To talk about how a word sounds, say: "Hendes udtale er god" (Her pronunciation is good).

en udvej.explanation: "En udvej" means "a way out". It is built from "ud" (out) and "en vej" (a road). To say you search for a solution, use it with "at finde" (to find): "at finde en udvej" (to find a way out).

en udveksling.explanation: "En udveksling" means "an exchange". To talk about a school or university stay abroad, it is part of "en udvekslingsstudent" (an exchange student).

en udvidelse.explanation: "En udvidelse" means "an expansion". To say a company grows, use the verb "at udvide" (to expand): "Firmaet vil udvide" (The company wants to expand).

en udvikler.explanation: "En udvikler" means "a developer". It comes from the verb "at udvikle" (to develop). To say what kind of developer, put a word in front: "en softwareudvikler" (a software developer).

en udvikling.explanation: "En udvikling" means "a development". It comes from the verb "at udvikle" (to develop). To say a place changes over time, use the verb with "sig" (itself): "Byen udvikler sig hurtigt" (The city is developing fast).

en uenighed.explanation: "En uenighed" means "a disagreement". The start "u-" turns a word into its opposite, as in "en enighed" (an agreement). To say that you personally disagree, use the adjective "uenig": "Jeg er uenig" (I disagree).

en uge.explanation: "En uge" means "a week". To say "next week", say: "Jeg rejser i næste uge" (I am traveling next week). To say "this week", say: "Jeg har travlt i denne uge" (I am busy this week). To name a week by its number, say: "uge 42" (week 42).

en ugeavis.explanation: "En ugeavis" means "a weekly local paper". It is built from "en uge" (a week) and "en avis" (a newspaper). To say where you read something, add "i" (in): "Det stod i ugeavisen" (It was in the weekly paper).

en ugedag.explanation: "En ugedag" means "a day of the week". It is built from "uge" (week) and "dag" (day). Inside a sentence, a day name is written without a capital, unlike in English: "mandag" (Monday).

en ugeplan.explanation: "En ugeplan" means "a weekly plan". It is built from "en uge" (a week) and "en plan" (a plan). To ask what is on it, say: "Hvad står der på ugeplanen?" (What does the weekly plan say?)

en ugle.explanation: "En ugle" means "an owl". To say a person stays up late, use "en natugle" (a night owl): "Min bror er en natugle" (My brother is a night owl).

en uklarhed.explanation: "En uklarhed" means "a lack of clarity". The start "u-" turns a word into its opposite, as in "en klarhed" (clarity). To say a text can be read in two ways, use "en tvetydighed" (an ambiguity) instead: "Sætningen har en tvetydighed" (The sentence has an ambiguity).

en uldsweater.explanation: "En uldsweater" means "a wool sweater". It is built from "uld" (wool) and "en sweater" (a sweater). To say a sweater is made of another fabric, change the first part: "en bomuldssweater" (a cotton sweater).

en ulempe.explanation: "En ulempe" means "a disadvantage". Its opposite is "en fordel" (an advantage), and the two come as a pair: "fordele og ulemper" (advantages and disadvantages).

en ultralydsscanning.explanation: "En ultralydsscanning" means "an ultrasound scan". It is built from "ultralyd" (ultrasound) and "en scanning" (a scan). A shorter way to say it is just "en scanning": "Jeg har en scanning i morgen" (I have a scan tomorrow).

en ulv.explanation: "En ulv" means "a wolf". To say someone gives a false alarm, use "at råbe ulv" (literally, to shout wolf): "Han råber ulv hele tiden" (He cries wolf all the time).

en ulykke.explanation: "En ulykke" means "an accident". It also means "misfortune": "Det er en stor ulykke for familien" (It is a great misfortune for the family). The start "u-" turns a word into its opposite, so it is built from "u-" and "lykke" (luck, happiness).

en undergang.explanation: "En undergang" means "a downfall". It is literally a going under, like the verb "at gå under" (to perish). To say something big comes to an end, use the verb: "Imperiet gik under" (The empire came to an end).

en underordnet.explanation: "En underordnet" means "a subordinate". The same word is used for something of lower rank: "en underordnet stilling" (a lower position).

en underskrift.explanation: "En underskrift" means "a signature". It is built from "under" (under) and "skrift" (writing), the writing under a text. To say you sign, use "at skrive under" (literally, to write under): "Jeg skriver under på aftalen" (I sign the agreement).

en undersøgelse.explanation: "En undersøgelse" means "an examination". To say you go for a check at the doctor, say: "Jeg skal til undersøgelse hos lægen" (I am going for an examination at the doctor). When researchers report findings, it means "a study": "Undersøgelsen viser, at mange sover for lidt" (The study shows that many people sleep too little).

en undertekst.explanation: "En undertekst" means "a subtitle". It is built from "under" (under) and "en tekst" (a text). To say a film has subtitles, use the plural: "Filmen har danske undertekster" (The movie has Danish subtitles).

en undertrøje.explanation: "En undertrøje" means "an undershirt". The start "under-" means "under", as in "en underkjole" (a slip).

en underviser.explanation: "En underviser" means "an instructor". It comes from the verb "at undervise" (to teach). To name a person who teaches children at school, use "en lærer" (a teacher) instead: "Min lærer hedder Anne" (My teacher is called Anne).

en undskyldning.explanation: "En undskyldning" means "an apology". It also means "an excuse", a reason you give for something that went wrong: "Han har altid en undskyldning for at komme for sent" (He always has an excuse for being late).

en undtagelse.explanation: "En undtagelse" means "an exception". To say who or what is left out, use "med undtagelse af" (with the exception of): "Alle kom med undtagelse af Lars" (Everyone came except Lars).

en uniform.explanation: "En uniform" means "a uniform". To name a uniform for school children, put a word in front: "en skoleuniform" (a school uniform).

en union.explanation: "En union" means "a union", as in a group of countries: "Den Europæiske Union" (the European Union). A workers' union is a different word, "en fagforening" (a trade union): "Jeg er medlem af en fagforening" (I am a member of a trade union).

en uregelmæssighed.explanation: "En uregelmæssighed" means "an irregularity". It is built from "uregelmæssig" (irregular), the same word as in "uregelmæssige verber" (irregular verbs).

en urmager.explanation: "En urmager" means "a watchmaker". It is built from "et ur" (a watch or clock) and "-mager" (maker). The ending "-mager" is also in "en skomager" (a shoemaker).

en urne.explanation: "En urne" means "an urn", as in the container for a person's ashes. A box for votes at an election is "en valgurne" (a ballot box): "Hun lægger sin stemme i valgurnen" (She puts her vote in the ballot box).

en usb-nøgle.explanation: "En USB-nøgle" means "a USB stick". Literally it is a USB key, since "en nøgle" means "a key".

en usikkerhed.explanation: "En usikkerhed" means "an uncertainty". The start "u-" turns a word into its opposite, as in "sikker" (sure). To say you feel unsure about yourself, use it with "at føle" (to feel): "Jeg føler usikkerhed, når jeg skal tale foran andre" (I feel uncertain when I have to speak in front of others).

et udbrud.explanation: "Et udbrud" means "an outbreak". When someone suddenly shows a strong feeling, it means "an outburst", used with "af" (of): "et udbrud af vrede" (an outburst of anger).

et udbud.explanation: "Et udbud" means "a supply", as in goods on the market. It also means "a tender", when a city or a company asks firms to compete for a job: "Kommunen har sendt byggeriet i udbud" (The municipality has put the construction work out to tender).

et udbytte.explanation: "Et udbytte" means "a yield / benefit". When a company pays money to the people who own its shares, it means "a dividend": "Firmaet udbetaler et udbytte" (The company pays out a dividend).

et udfald.explanation: "Et udfald" means "an outcome". To say which event has the outcome, add "af" (of): "udfaldet af kampen" (the outcome of the match).

et udflugtsmål.explanation: "Et udflugtsmål" means "a destination for an outing". It is built from "en udflugt" (an outing) and "et mål" (a goal). In sports, "et mål" also means a goal: "Han scorede et mål" (He scored a goal).

et udgangspunkt.explanation: "Et udgangspunkt" means "a starting point". To say you start from something, use "at tage udgangspunkt i" (to start from): "Lad os tage udgangspunkt i tallene" (Let us start from the numbers).

et udkast.explanation: "Et udkast" means "a draft". It is built from "ud" (out) and "et kast" (a throw). To ask to see an early version, say: "Må jeg se udkastet?" (May I see the draft?)

et udråbstegn.explanation: "Et udråbstegn" means "an exclamation mark". It is built from "udråb" (an exclamation) and "et tegn" (a sign).

et udsagn.explanation: "Et udsagn" means "a statement". To say that what someone claims is true, say: "Hans udsagn er sandt" (His statement is true). Do not mix it up with "en udtalelse" (an official statement): "Ministeren gav en udtalelse" (The minister gave a statement).

et udsagnsord.explanation: "Et udsagnsord" means "a verb". It is built from "et udsagn" (a statement) and "et ord" (a word). In a dictionary, a verb is listed with "at" (to) in front: "at spise" (to eat).

et udsalg.explanation: "Et udsalg" means "a sale". To say a store has a sale, use it with "at have" (to have): "Butikken har udsalg" (The store has a sale). To talk about one item at a special price, use "et tilbud" (an offer) instead: "Der er tilbud på mælk" (Milk is on offer).

et udseende.explanation: "Et udseende" means "an appearance". It comes from the verb "at se ud" (to look). To describe how someone looks, use the verb: "Hun ser træt ud" (She looks tired).

et udsigtspunkt.explanation: "Et udsigtspunkt" means "a viewpoint". It is built from "en udsigt" (a view) and "et punkt" (a point).

et udslip.explanation: "Et udslip" means "a leak". For a spill of oil, put a word in front: "et olieudslip" (an oil spill).

et udslæt.explanation: "Et udslæt" means "a rash". To say someone got a rash, you can leave out "et": "Han fik udslæt" (He got a rash).

et udspil.explanation: "Et udspil" means "a proposal". In card games, it means the first card played: "Hvem har udspillet?" (Who has the lead?)

et udtryk.explanation: "Et udtryk" means "an expression". When you talk about the look on someone's face, put "ansigts-" (face) in front: "et ansigtsudtryk" (a facial expression).

et uheld.explanation: "Et uheld" means "an accident / bad luck". To say something happened by mistake, use "ved et uheld" (by accident): "Glasset gik i stykker ved et uheld" (The glass broke by accident). A serious crash with injuries is "en ulykke" (an accident): "Der var en ulykke på motorvejen" (There was an accident on the highway).

et underholdningsprogram.explanation: "Et underholdningsprogram" means "an entertainment show". It is built from "underholdning" (entertainment) and "et program" (a program).

et underskud.explanation: "Et underskud" means "a deficit". Its opposite is "et overskud" (a surplus): "Firmaet har et overskud" (The company has a surplus). When you say you have energy left for other people or tasks, you also use "overskud": "Jeg har ikke overskud i dag" (I have no energy to spare today).

et ungdomshus.explanation: "Et ungdomshus" means "a youth center". It is built from "ungdom" (youth) and "et hus" (a house).

et ungdomskort.explanation: "Et ungdomskort" means "a youth travel pass". It is built from "ungdom" (youth) and "et kort" (a card). "Et kort" also means a map: "et kort over byen" (a map of the city).

et univers.explanation: "Et univers" means "a universe". To talk about the whole world of an author or a film, use it for that world: "forfatterens univers" (the author's universe).

et universitet.explanation: "Et universitet" means "a university". To say you study a subject there, use "at læse" (to read): "Jeg læser biologi" (I study biology).

et upload.explanation: "Et upload" means "an upload". It comes from the verb "at uploade" (to upload). To say you do it, use the verb: "Jeg uploader filen" (I upload the file).
